sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Base parts and submenu trigger
sections.what: Imports the libraries and gives the base parts short names. Builds the row that opens a submenu, with a small arrow on the right.
sections.why: Likely reason: sets up the base parts and the nested-menu row style.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Main menu box and clickable rows
sections.what: Builds the floating menu box that opens below its button and the standard rows inside it. Rows highlight when focused and dim when disabled.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the main box and rows their shared look.
sections.watch_out: The default gap below the button is set here, so changing it moves every dropdown.

sections.name: File setup (part 3)
sections.title: Checkbox and radio options
sections.what: Builds rows that show a check mark or a dot when selected, and a regular row style for them.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows selection state inside the menu.

sections.name: File setup (part 4)
sections.title: Labels, dividers, shortcut text, and exports
sections.what: Builds the group label text, the divider line, and the small shortcut hint on the right. The final list makes all parts available to other files.
sections.why: Likely reason: organizes entries and shows key hints.
sections.watch_out: The shortcut hint is display only and does not run any action.

summary: Builds the styled pieces of a dropdown menu, which opens from a button when clicked. It includes the menu box, rows, checkboxes, radio options, labels, dividers, submenus, and shortcut hint text.
purpose: Gives every click-to-open menu in the app the same look. It is the button-triggered sibling of the right-click menu file.
why: Likely reason: a shared look keeps menus consistent. The code does not state this directly.
how: It imports the dropdown library, icon set, and style helper. It gives each base part a DropdownMenu name and wraps the ones that need styling. The main box sits a small gap below its button by default. It then exports all the parts.
inputs: Settings from the screen: style overrides, an indent flag, checked state for checkboxes, the gap from the button, and standard element settings.
outputs: Components that show a click-to-open menu. Nothing is stored.
risks: Visual changes only. Changing the default gap or the divider color changes every dropdown in the app. Behavior such as closing on outside click comes from the library.
debug: If the menu does not open, check the button and its screen code. If spacing looks off, check the default gap in the main box wrapper. Some long style strings were cut off in the copy I was given.
